Question: \(\frac{\sin10^\circ+\sin20^\circ}{\cos10^\circ+\cos20^\circ}\) equals
Solution:
The angles \(10^\circ\) and \(20^\circ\) lie equally far from \(15^\circ\). Writing them as \(15^\circ-5^\circ\) and \(15^\circ+5^\circ\) lets the terms involving \(\sin5^\circ\) cancel in the addition formulas:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin10^\circ+\sin20^\circ
&=\sin(15^\circ-5^\circ)+\sin(15^\circ+5^\circ)\\
&=2\sin15^\circ\cos5^\circ,\\
\cos10^\circ+\cos20^\circ
&=\cos(15^\circ-5^\circ)+\cos(15^\circ+5^\circ)\\
&=2\cos15^\circ\cos5^\circ.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both \(\cos5^\circ\) and \(\cos15^\circ\) are positive because their angles are acute. The denominator is therefore nonzero, and cancellation gives
\[
\frac{2\sin15^\circ\cos5^\circ}{2\cos15^\circ\cos5^\circ}
=\frac{\sin15^\circ}{\cos15^\circ}
=\boxed{\tan15^\circ},
\]
choice D.
